statement: On-hand when differing repeated rows of one key are summed (N-0110, D-0091 names units only). Question: how do on-hand, in transit and on order combine? Options: (1) a value every line repeats is one snapshot and kept once, different values are summed (built); (2) always sum; (3) keep the last line's. Evidence on cip: 73 repeated rows carry on-hand; 69 repeat one value (Takealot: a week split over two months, each line 336), 4 differ (Computer Mania, two article rows per product: on-hand +168). Assumption: equal values on split lines are the same stock. Impact: option 2 would double Takealot on-hand. Reversible: re-apply the loads. Resolving experiment: ask Computer Mania whether its two article rows hold separate stock.
